payload.claim: No test for `batch_spend` (or `close_batch`, which derives its stored spend through it) ever populates a second batch's attempts in the same ledger. `test_closing_a_batch_derives_and_stores_its_spend` and `test_a_running_batchs_spend_is_readable_before_it_closes` each create exactly one batch with real attempt costs, so `saffron/ledger.py`'s `WHERE r.batch_id = ?` filter (line 432) could be deleted entirely — summing every attempt ever recorded in the ledger instead of one batch's — and both tests would still pass, since there is nothing else in the tiny fresh `tmp_path` ledger to sum. In production the ledger is one file accumulating every batch a repo has ever run (per `SCHEMA`'s own comment), so this is exactly the case where a fixture-only assumption (one batch's worth of rows exist) masks a cross-batch leak that would make every night's budget gate see the wrong, ever-growing total. `test_a_batchs_runs_are_readable_from_the_batch` already shows the pattern needed (a second batch with its own run) but it is never applied to a batch with attempts/spend.
